extracted.intended_audience: public sector managers, administrators and work teams responsible for administrative decision‑making and PAJA compliance in government institutions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implementation tools for identifying, mapping, analysing and amending administrative decisions to ensure compliance with the Promotion of Administrative Justice Act (PAJA). Aimed at teams in government units who must mainstream PAJA into business processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: A decision
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be a decision (an act of deciding — to do something, not to do something, or to tolerate something).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: an administrator’s choice to award a tender or to refuse an application. A finding that a department decided to do something qualifies as a decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative nature made in terms of an empowering provision
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision must be of an administrative nature and made in terms of an empowering provision (i.e. the power to make the decision is given by statute or other empowering provision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the empowering provision for any particular procedures or steps and verify that the decision is within the scope (e.g., spending public money under the PFMA gives a department the power to award tenders). Also check lawfulness by reference to the empowering provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not specifically excluded by PAJA
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision must not fall within any of PAJA’s express exclusions (i.e. it must not be specifically excluded by section 1/exclusions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When determining whether a decision is an administrative action, compare it against PAJA’s exclusion list; if it fits an exclusion it is not an administrative action for PAJA purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Made by an organ of state
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision must be made by an organ of state (including departments at national, provincial and municipal level; functionaries or institutions exercising statutory powers; and private individuals/companies when exercising public power).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify whether the actor is an organ of state or a private actor exercising public power; this determines PAJA coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adversely affects rights
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision must adversely affect the rights of someone or a group — i.e. have a negative effect (eg. refuse, limit or remove rights, or decide someone does not have a right).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A beneficial/favourable decision is not an administrative action under PAJA. Example: awarding a tender is favourable to the successful bidder (not adversely affected) but adverse for the unsuccessful bidders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Has direct external legal effect (three components)
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision must have direct external legal effect, comprising: (a) legal effect — be legally binding; (b) direct effect — be the final step that affects members of the public; (c) external effect — affect someone outside the organ of state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a process requires multiple internal steps and only the final step affects the public, only that final step is an administrative action. Verify legal bindingness and that the effect falls on external persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritise and list administrative decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and list administrative decisions made in the business unit and prioritise which administrative decisions should be analysed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Think about core business processes; use the list to select decisions for mapping and PAJA testing. Prioritisation helps focus analysis on key/high‑impact decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult legal advisors for difficult determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult the institution’s legal advisors when uncertain about whether a listed decision is an administrative action or other PAJA issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal advice is encouraged when applying the PAJA criteria to specific decisions or interpreting empowering provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map the decision‑making process
rubrics_metrics.description: Map the current decision‑making process (the process known and followed by personnel), ideally in a formal format or standard operating procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include process/activity, symbols (ovals for start/end, boxes for tasks, diamonds for decision points, arrows for direction), deliverables, inputs/outputs. Use A4/post‑its for group mapping, nominate a facilitator, and be prepared to iterate the map.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check whether empowering provision prescribes procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Check if the empowering provision sets out a particular procedure or steps to be followed and verify consistency between practice and the empowering provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the statute prescribes steps, ensure institutional practice matches. Inconsistency may signal non‑compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliverables clearly indicated in process maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Process maps should clearly indicate deliverables when a detailed procedure map is produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label outputs so it is clear what the end products of each activity are; useful for compliance and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify gaps for PAJA compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify gaps in the current decision‑making process by checking for PAJA compliance (e.g., missing notices, lack of reasons, failure to allow participation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As you map the process, compare each step against PAJA mandatory procedures and other PAJA requirements to find where the process fails to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonableness — decisions must be justifiable
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision must be reasonable: the decision taken must be justifiable and based on good reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the decision‑making process is thorough, identify and check factors, and document reasoning so outcomes are supportable; unreasonable process may be reviewable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and take into account relevant factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors relevant to the decision must be identified, checked and taken into account when making decisions and evaluating alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document which factors were considered and ensure irrelevant factors were excluded; failure to consider relevant factors may render a decision unreasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Before‑decision: adequate notice of nature and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the decision is taken, affected persons must receive adequate notice of the nature and purpose of the proposed administrative action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications (letters, forms, adverts) should explain what decision is being planned and why, and include how affected persons can participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Before‑decision: reasonable opportunity to make representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected persons must be given a reasonable opportunity to make representations (to object, provide information, etc.) before the decision is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable timeframes may vary; the institution should set and publish clear timeframes for participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: After‑decision: clear statement of administrative action
rubrics_metrics.description: After the decision is taken, communications should contain a clear statement of the administrative action and the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the decision is communicated clearly and understandably in writing, using language the applicant will understand.

rubrics_metrics.name: After‑decision: notice of right to request reasons (Section 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected persons must be informed of the right to request reasons in terms of Section 5 of PAJA (and be provided reasons where appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good administrative practice is to provide reasons at the time the decision is communicated; if reasons are not given, provide notice of the right to request reasons and how to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: After‑decision: notice of right to internal appeal or review
rubrics_metrics.description: Affected persons must be informed of their right to appeal internally (if an internal appeal exists) or of their right to seek judicial review, including steps and timeframes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide information on where to lodge an appeal, forms required, contact details, and time limits. If no internal appeal exists, explain judicial review options and applicable courts/timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication must be clear and understandable
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications of decisions are expected to be written in a manner that the applicant will understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid legalese where practicable; state outcomes, rights, remedies and next steps plainly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframes must be reasonable and documented
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be a clear and reasonable timeframe for participation and for processes; timeframes should be written into decision‑making procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeframes will differ by circumstance but must be defensible; publish or include timeframes in documentation and invitations to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability — administrators must be able to explain decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrators must be accountable for the use of public power and able to explain decisions to affected people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain records, reasoning, and communication so that the institution can demonstrate accountability if challenged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use discretion to allow rectification of inadvertent omissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there are clear, justifiable reasons, officials should use discretion to afford applicants (e.g., bidders) an opportunity to rectify inadvertent omissions or inaccuracies rather than strictly eliminating them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rigid approach that always eliminates for minor/formal omissions may be reviewable on grounds of unreasonableness under PAJA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide templates and standardised letters to address gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt standardised letter templates (eg. to notify unsuccessful bidders) that include notice of rights to request reasons and to seek review/appeal, or state when reasons will be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Templates can be customised; include contact names, addresses (email/fax/post), what to include in a request (name, telephone, mailing address) and deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for requesting reasons and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify accessible methods by which affected persons can request reasons or lodge appeals (email, fax, registered mail, hand delivery) and provide the appropriate addresses and contact details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include instructions to include identifying information and contact details in the request; provide alternatives if applicants cannot travel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self‑assessment and progress indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Use self‑assessment tools to confirm progress before moving phases: team understands PAJA elements, has identified administrative decisions, mapped processes, considered all inputs, analysed for PAJA compliance, identified gaps and proposed recommendations, and obtained approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the listed progress indicators as a checklist to decide readiness to proceed to the next phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amend decision‑making processes and obtain management approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Turn recommendations into amended decision‑making processes, forms and letters to ensure PAJA compliance and obtain management approval to effect changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Information Sheet 5 (examples of wording for templates) and Information Sheet 6 (database of examples) to draft changes; secure approval before implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check after‑decision communications for required content
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing after‑decision communications, check they inform the affected person whether they were informed of the decision, provided reasons or informed of the right to request reasons, and informed of rights of review/appeal and associated procedures/timeframes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any of these elements are missing, identify as a gap and remedy (eg. standardised letters, templates, or alternative methods of notifying outcomes).
